referenceSize.note: Aquarium colony width; wild Acropora colonies reach 1 m to several metres across (AIMS Coral Fact Sheets, Corals of the World), so 15 cm is a grown frag / small display colony. Measured across the whole mesh including corallites and extended polyps.

morphology.notes: Colony of closed branch tubes with axial corallites at every tip (swollen lip, recessed calice) and appressed radial corallites (small tubes, pointing distally) along the branches, each with a six tentacle polyp. Form is selected per variant: staghorn (arborescent), table (tabular plate with upright branchlets on a stalk), bushy (digitate fingers on a broad mound), hairy (A. millepora style corymbose cushion of short thick branchlets under a dense field of long extended polyps). Sizes below are design centimetres; the colony is scaled so the xy width equals referenceSize.

animation.note: Stony coral rule: the skeleton never moves. Base, trunk, plate, branches and corallite tubes are weighted 1.0 to the Base bone, which is never a channel target; the rig has no other bones. Only the polyp crowns move, through morph targets on the per-cluster crown meshes: polypLean bends the tentacle tips downstream (roots stay in the calice), polypFlutter drives two interleaved halves of every crown field (flutterA / flutterB) sideways along per-polyp seeded directions at different phases, polypRetract folds the tentacles into the calice. Pulse waveforms are unipolar and exactly zero at the loop seam; clip order matters: the looping sway clip is declared last so the validators leave the colony at its rest silhouette.

visualDebt: Polyps carry six tentacle tubes instead of the twelve of a real Acropora polyp (LOD1 triangle budget).

Only the prominent radial corallites are modelled (up to eleven per branch, some dropped where a neighbouring branch is too close); the dense field of small radials is carried by the texture relief and roughness.
Corallites are flared tubes with a recessed calice; the nariform (longer lower lip) profile and the septa are texture only.
The tabular plate is a lobed, radially ridged solid lens rather than a perforated mesh of anastomosing horizontal branchlets.
Retraction folds the tentacles to about half length (0.3 of the length on the hairy form) rather than fully into the calice.

Polyp crowns are one rigid unskinned mesh per branch cluster with morph targets rather than skinned geometry; this works around a glTF importer and runtime-gate interaction, see the lane shared-change-request. Per-polyp variation comes from seeded tentacle geometry, per-polyp flutter directions and two interleaved flutter halves per cluster, not from independent per-polyp phases.
The hairy form is the digitate layout with short thick branchlets; A. millepora's plate-like fused base and the coenosteum spinules are texture only.
